stemMd: A restriction enzyme recognises a particular short DNA sequence. What determines where it cuts a DNA molecule?

options.label: B
options.textMd: The mass of the entire organism

options.label: D
options.textMd: The amino-acid sequence of every cellular protein

options.label: E
options.textMd: The positions of its recognition sequence

explanationMd: Sequence-specific recognition places cuts at defined DNA sites. This permits reproducible DNA fragments and is useful in recombinant-DNA methods; it is not a random cut based on cell size or appearance.

distractorRationale.c: Ribosomes translate RNA rather than determine these sites.
distractorRationale.a: Colour does not define restriction sites.
distractorRationale.d: The enzyme recognises DNA, not all cellular proteins.
distractorRationale.b: Recognition is local to DNA sequence.
